3.q: Trace the correct sequence of developments that carried European sailors from the 1453 route blockage to the open-ocean voyage to India.
3.a: The maritime chain runs: (1) The Ottoman capture of Constantinople blocks the overland Silk Route (2) Spice prices soar under mercantilist competition (3) The caravel with lateen sails and the magnetic compass make open-ocean sailing possible (4) Portuguese captains sail directly to India and bypass the middlemen. A wrong answer that credits the Industrial Revolution or the East India Company shows the student has missed the chronological trigger in West Asia and the two navigational innovations that turned a spice crisis into the Age of Discovery.

4.q: Trace the correct sequence of changes by which Goa's capture in 1510 transformed the Portuguese presence in India.
4.a: The transformation runs: (1) Vasco da Gama lands at Calicut in 1498 opening the direct sea route (2) Temporary trade factories operate under the sufferance of local rulers (3) Afonso de Albuquerque seizes Goa as a secure headquarters (4) Goa gains shipyards and mints as the Estado da India base projecting power across the Arabian Sea. A wrong answer that treats Goa as just another trading post shows the student has missed the shift from vulnerable factories to permanent sovereign territorial control.
